doc.title: Nat Hentoff interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007

title: Ben Webster's credo: when the rhythm section ain't making it
summary: Ben Webster, playing a single without his rhythm section, swung the band and gave Hentoff a lifetime credo.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Well you did it very well. There’s something about this, jazz musicians, you called them your rabbis?

Well growing up, I mean, I was still in my very early twenties and Ben Webster, who had left Duke Ellington, much to his later regret, was on the road and most of the places he © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

played as a single couldn’t afford his regular rhythm section. So we were in a club and the rhythm section was trying but they weren’t making it. So Ben swung the band. And in between sets we were sitting at the bar and he gave me a lifetime credo. He said when the rhythm section ain’t making it, go for yourself. And I do that with editors sometimes.
